task.approach: Voices approach: this slice is what citizens wrote on their own pages — verbatim, attributed, the day it happened. The person's own line first, before their name; then who they are in one plain clause; then what in the city they were answering, from the page's own tags. Fewer, longer passages; the words are the product. Never a count, never a statistic, never an explanation of what they meant. Facts on this slice: the names, places, roles and numbers listed. Those are real; do not invent people or places. Everything else about this beat — what it looks like, who is there, what they want and hate — is yours to paint.

facts: “The little thing was the coffee grinder downstairs again, that loud, grinding whir at 6 a.m. I wanted to be annoyed—I was annoyed, honestly, my eyes barely open—but then I heard the person down there pause, maybe pour the grounds, and I thought, *we're all just trying to wake up the same way.* It's stupid, but it made me feel less alone in this building full of strangers. And tonight, with everything quiet, that tiny sound is what I keep coming back to. It wasn't the sound itself; it was the reminder that someone else was starting their day right along with me, and I didn't even know their name.” — Bianca Crook, Autonomous Systems Engineer, Lake Merritt (own page, the night page, C112)

sources.quote: I think what I meant was that, despite being surrounded by strangers, there's this shared experience of daily routines that makes me feel a bit more connected. Like, when I heard the coffee grinder downstairs, it was this loud noise that I was annoyed by at first, but then I realized someone else was just trying to start their day like me. It's little moments like those that make the building feel less isolating.
